punchline: Your brain would rather hand you a convincing reason than admit it has no idea.
thirty_sec: Some epilepsy patients have the link between their brain's hemispheres surgically cut. In the lab, an image shown only to the right hemisphere lets the left hand pick the matching object. But the left hemisphere, which does the talking, never saw the image. Instead of saying 'I don't know,' it invents a fluent, confident, false reason. Researchers call it the interpreter, and David Eagleman argues it's running in all of us, narrating choices it didn't make.
question: When you tell someone why you made a choice, how sure are you that the reason is what actually caused it?
